coverage.assessment: The snowball mechanism and the escalation to stones are cut, so the injury and violence lack their setup (F1). In the coalition, the statesman-versus-machine contrast is removed despite a planned reduced form (F3).

'The second step led to the White House' has no named first step (F5). In P4, 'raggedness of a new kind' has lost its point of comparison (F7). Brother Charles, the gallery, the dining-room run and the ages all remain clear.
The chapter has little dialogue. The aunt's dry remark, Cushing's misheard phrase with its correction, and the telling of Sumner are attributed correctly.

Three source qualifiers are dropped: Henry was never actually in a mob, the family was at home in the White House except under Jackson, and respect for Washington was only 'to all appearance' sincere (F2). Alley's claim stays attributed to Alley, and the dates and ages are correct.

The retrospective framing survives in the Savage/Marvin line, the 'in later life' doubt over the ribbon and the 1904 look back. There is no premature disclosure, and the Civil War is limited to the allowed phrasings.

Two deflating cadences are removed: 'bravado passed unnoticed; no one even cuffed his ears' and the return to 'George Washington stood alone' (F4). Several compressions flatten texture without breaking sense (F6).

Cutting 'Boy as he was, he knew enough to know that something was wrong' simplifies the moral confusion (F3). The closing loses the reasonable/unreasonable framing of the West and the boy's self-satisfaction before the reversal (F8).
Four dependencies are intact at both endpoints. The Cunard echo is weakened because partner 007 no longer names the Cunard Line or Judkins; this is not a fault of chapter 005.

strengths: The Conky Daniels climax and the Savage/Marvin retrospective line are kept intact, including Henry staying only because Charles was too big to run.
The 'memory, not actual journey' qualification flagged as a risk in the plan is preserved verbatim.
V4, V5, V6 and V7 survive in sequence, so the Washington paradox maps onto the Sumner paradox and leads to 'Tammany Hall stood at the end of the vista'.
The gallery mishearing with its correction, the April 24, 1851 vote, and the white ribbon against black crepe all remain intact.
summary: The revision keeps most of the chapter's architecture: all eight verbatim passages, the doubled response to slavery, the Pole Star, the coalition epigrams, the gallery scene, the ribbon, the Cunard smoke and the hedged year‑1 close. Every continuity check holds. Its further cuts go beyond the first draft, though. Most seriously, every reference to snow is gone from the 'snowball war', so the stone injury is no longer explained by a stone hidden in a snowball. The cuts also strip several qualifiers (no actual mob; the Jackson exception; 'to all appearance sincerely'), the planned 'subordinates ran the machine' contrast, the boy's admission that 'something was wrong', and a few comic deflations. A 'second step' with no first step dangles from the first draft.
